Mina / Marissa — quick technical/legal notes ahead of drafting:

1) Transfer mechanism: For EU -> US flows we default to the latest EU SCCs for processor-to-processor transfers and maintain a documented Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA). We also offer contract terms that permit customers to require EU-only residency for persisted logs and index shards on Dedicated/Private deployments.

2) DPF status: DPF (Data Privacy Framework) is not used as our sole mechanism for transferring regulated personal data at this time; where customers want DPF-specific attestations we can provide the operational evidentiary artifacts we hold, but SCCs + TIA remain the primary legal tool.

3) Processor role & sub-processors: Redwood operates as a processor. Our sub-processor roster includes cloud infra providers, a managed database provider for metadata storage, and a telemetry ingestion partner. We publish a current CSV and provide 30 days' notice prior to material additions — unless emergency operational needs require a shorter timeframe and we notify promptly.

4) Technical controls evidence: Marissa — can you assemble the following artifacts for the ZenitCare pack?
   - network diagram showing EU-region tenancy and egress controls (PDF)
   - KV cache retention and encryption notes (short doc)
   - sample audit log extract demonstrating retention & access controls (redacted)
   - list of encryption-at-rest algorithms and KMS integrations (short summary)

I will draft the DPA annex redline focusing on SCC references, breach notification SLA, and sub-processor flow-down clauses.

Karthik
Director, Legal — Privacy & Contracts
